editor_note: Neither rewritten entry would mislead a learner. Entry 6 keeps the meaning of the Paulice announcement: low-overhead error detection (낮은 오버헤드의 양자 오류 감지), single-shot access (단일 샷 액세스), and use in both sampling-based and expectation-value-based workflows. Entry 10 says '오류 민감도 상한을 더 엄격하게 한정합니다'. This makes 'bound' an explicit upper bound (상한), which is defensible, but '상한을 … 한정' is redundant and stiff, and '표적화된 방식으로' reads like a calque. Both entries also use the formal 합니다/습니다 endings (소개합니다, 있습니다, 한정합니다) instead of the project's 해요체 convention.

examples.source: uses classical simulations to more tightly bound the sensitivity to errors throughout the circuit ... more efficient, targeted applications of Probabilistic Error Cancellation (PEC)
examples.translation: Circuit 전반의 오류 민감도 상한을 더 엄격하게 한정합니다 ... 더 효율적이고 표적화된 방식으로 적용할 수 있습니다
examples.suggested: 회로 전반의 오류 민감도에 대해 더 촘촘한 상한을 구해요 ... PEC를 더 효율적이고 필요한 곳에 집중해 적용할 수 있어요
examples.why: '상한을 한정하다' is redundant, and '표적화된' is a stiff calque of 'targeted'. The meaning is still intact.

examples.source: Introducing Qiskit Paulice ... can be used in both sampling-based and expectation value-based workflows.
examples.why: The project convention is 해요체. These entries use the formal 합니다/습니다 endings, a formal-register slip.

editor_note: Both rewritten entries are faithful: [35] keeps "Sharpe ratio versus return" as "수익률 대비 샤프 비율", keeps "100큐비트 이상", and keeps the hedged "초기 사용자들은 … 탐색하고 있습니다", and [41] renders the future commitment as "앞으로 몇 주에 걸쳐 … 제공하게 됩니다", in the same register as the rest of the page.
The translation is faithful and reads naturally. "changelog" is rendered as "변경 로그", and entry [5] correctly says the skill "코드 마이그레이션을 위해 릴리스되었습니다" in consistent 합니다체, which matches the source.

The meaning is faithful throughout. The hedge in [9] ("might be faster" → "더 빠르고 더 나은 결과를 낼 수 있는") and the AI-pass claim both survive, and 트랜스파일/트랜스파일러 패스 are used consistently. The project convention is 해요체, but the declarative sentences use formal 합니다체: [0] 포함합니다, and in [9] 제공합니다 (twice) and 것입니다. The imperatives (참조하세요, 방문하세요, 읽어보세요) are fine.

examples.source: The latest updates from Qiskit Transpiler Service client, including the latest package release summaries and platform updates.
examples.translation: Qiskit Transpiler Service client의 최신 업데이트로, 최신 패키지 릴리스 요약 및 플랫폼 업데이트를 포함합니다.

examples.why: It uses 합니다체 where the project uses 해요체. This is a formal-register slip.

examples.source: Perhaps most importantly, the service invites users to experiment with new and improved AI-powered transpiler passes — cutting-edge tools that might be faster ...
examples.translation: ... 직접 실험해 볼 수 있다는 것입니다. 이는 전통적인 트랜스파일 방법보다 더 빠르고 더 나은 결과를 낼 수 있는 최첨단 도구입니다.
examples.suggested: ... 직접 실험해 볼 수 있다는 점이에요. 이 패스들은 기존 트랜스파일 방법보다 더 빠르고 더 나은 결과를 낼 수 있는 최첨단 도구예요.
examples.why: 제공합니다, 것입니다 and 도구입니다 are formal 합니다체, not 해요체. Also, 기존 reads more naturally than 전통적인 for 'traditional methods' here.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. For example, "joint projective measurement" becomes 결합 사영 측정 and "early fault-tolerant targets" becomes 초기 결함 허용 타겟. The body prose uses the formal 합니다체 (포함합니다, 제공합니다, 있습니다) where the project convention is 해요체. The date heading [5] "January 2026" was left untranslated and should be 2026년 1월.

examples.why: The visible date heading is still in English. Only the anchor needs to stay in English.

examples.source: The latest updates from Qiskit SDK, including the latest package release summaries and platform updates.

examples.why: This is formal 합니다체 rather than the project's 해요체. The same register slip repeats in entries 6, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12.

editor_note: None of the 9 rewritten entries would mislead a reader. The quantities (68 ns vs 138 ns median, ~350 µs T1/T2), the On-Prem exception in entry 162, the deprecation and upgrade advice in entry 285, and the "experimental option" qualifier in entry 289 all carry over faithfully. The one issue is in entry 86. "fleet-leading coherence" became "유사하게 시스템 내 최고 수준의 코히어런스". Putting "유사하게" first as an adverb blurs the comparison with ibm_miami, and "시스템 내" reads as "within a system" rather than "across IBM's fleet". Entries 240, 279 and 285 use a formal 합니다체 register, not 해요체. That is consistent with the rest of this changelog, so I have not counted it as a defect.

examples.source: while maintaining similar fleet-leading coherence (T$_1$ of ~350 µs)
examples.translation: 유사하게 시스템 내 최고 수준의 코히어런스(T$_1$ ~350 µs)를 유지하면서
examples.suggested: `ibm_miami`와 비슷한 수준의, 전체 시스템 중 최고 수준 코히어런스(T$_1$ ~350 µs)를 유지하면서
examples.why: Putting 유사하게 first as an adverb hides what it is similar to (ibm_miami). 시스템 내 suggests 'within one system' when the source means 'best across the whole fleet'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing would mislead a learner. The beta caveat and the "0.47.0 이상" requirement in [11], the resilience_level note in [7] and the QDC 2025 preview claim in [5] are all intact. The declarative prose uses 합니다체 (포함합니다, 제공합니다, 발표하게 되어 기쁩니다, 보여줍니다, 릴리스되었습니다), which breaks the site's 해요체 convention; the imperatives (참조하세요, 확인하세요) are already fine. In [6], "이들은 … 을 구성하며, 이는 … 제공합니다" is a stiff calque of the English relative clause and would read better split into two sentences.

examples.translation: ... 출시를 발표하게 되어 기쁩니다. 두 가지 모두 QDC 2025에서 처음 공개되었습니다.

examples.why: The file uses 합니다체, but the project convention is 해요체. This is a register slip, not a meaning error.

examples.source: Together with Samplomatic, they make up the directed execution model, which provides full transparency and control to fine-tune your error mitigation workflow.
